official.application_cycle: Summer semester of the academic year 2026/2027; the programme runs two rounds a year (30 April and 31 October)
official.status_note: The call for applications for the summer semester of the academic year 2026/2027 is open; the online deadline is 31 October 2026 at 16:00 CET, and the stay may start between 1 February 2027 and 1 April 2027 for students (31 August 2027 for PhD students, teachers, researchers and artists)
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship is intended to cover the scholarship holder's living costs, i.e. the costs related to staying in Slovakia (food, accommodation, etc.); tuition coverage is not provided
benefits: 620 EUR monthly for university students of the second level of higher education (incoming track)
1025.50 EUR monthly for PhD students (incoming track)
1025.50 / 1370 / 1470 EUR monthly for university teachers, researchers and artists according to PhD degree and years of professional experience (incoming track)
Travel grant as a lump sum from 50 to 1500 EUR depending on the distance between home and host, for students and PhD students and for outgoing applicants resident in Slovakia
Reimbursement of medical examination costs up to 250 EUR for scholarship holders from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland whose stay exceeds 90 days and who need a temporary residence permit

Outgoing track: monthly rates approved per country, e.g. Czech Republic 600/750/850, Germany 930/1100/1250, United Kingdom 1150/1400/1500, United States 1900/2100/2200, Switzerland 2000/2100/2200 EUR for student/doctoral/postdoctoral categories
eligibility: Citizens of any country in the world, except citizens of Slovakia, can apply for a scholarship stay in Slovakia in the framework of the NSP

Students: university students outside Slovakia, of the second level of higher education or with at least 2.5 years of studies completed in the same/similar programme, accepted by a Slovak public, private or state higher education institution for academic mobility

PhD students: higher education or scientific training taking place outside Slovakia, accepted by a Slovak higher education institution or research institution entitled to run doctoral programmes (e.g. the Slovak Academy of Sciences) for a study/research/artistic stay

University teachers, researchers and artists: invited to a teaching/research/artistic stay by an institution seated in Slovakia holding a valid certificate of eligibility for research and development that is not a business company

Not supported: applicants accepted for full degree studies in Slovakia; applicants who spent 15 or more months in Slovakia within the 36 months before the deadline; applicants holding another publicly funded scholarship for the same stay; teachers/researchers/artists without a PhD and more than 4 years of experience (exceptionally accepted up to 7 years, at the lower rate)
Re-applying is only possible if at least 2 years have passed since the deadline by which the last NSP scholarship was awarded and received
requirements: Application submitted online by the deadline; the online system opens at least 6 weeks before the deadline and only one application per applicant per deadline is allowed

Applications and attachments in Slovak or English only; documents in other languages require an official translation, or a translation certified by the issuing institution (documents issued in Czech need no translation)
Acceptance/invitation letters and recommendation letters must not be older than 3 months on the day of the application deadline
The original of the acceptance/invitation letter must be physically delivered to SAIA, n.o. in Bratislava no later than the 3rd working day after the deadline, by 12:00

Before the first payment: letter of acceptance of the scholarship, a notarised copy of the diploma of the highest academic degree achieved, and confirmation of studies valid for the academic year of the stay
The scholarship is paid in monthly instalments to a bank account, usually in a SEPA country, after the account details and confirmation of the start of the stay are received
documents: Detailed study/research/artistic programme naming the Slovak host institution, start date, duration and time plan (with the list of subjects and credits for study stays)
Two recommendation letters from university teachers (students) or a recommendation from the dissertation supervisor (PhD students), signed and issued within 3 months
Confirmation of studies from the home institution issued within 3 months, with bachelor's/master's diploma, diploma supplement and state examination certificate where applicable

Acceptance/invitation letter of the Slovak host institution stating the period of stay; PhD students, teachers, researchers and artists also submit the list of publications/artistic activities in the prescribed structure
selection_criteria: Justification of why the applicant chose the selected Slovak host institution
Programme of the stay and how its results will be used for further studies, a scientific career or career development
Professional and personal qualities of the applicant, as assessed in the recommendation letters
Overall quality and consistency of the application, within the financial possibilities of the programme for the given deadline
coverage: Living costs, i.e. the costs related to staying in Slovakia (food, accommodation, etc.), during the study, research/artistic or teaching stay
Travel allowance paid as a lump sum by distance between the applicant's home and the Slovak host, for students and PhD students and for outgoing applicants resident in Slovakia
Medical examination reimbursement up to 250 EUR per scholarship holder (non-EU/EEA/Switzerland citizens with stays over 90 days)
Tuition is not covered by the scholarship
application_method: International applicants apply online at www.scholarships.sk; applicants from Slovakia apply online at www.stipendia.sk
The online application is completed and submitted with the SEND button once all fields are filled and all mandatory attachments uploaded
The original acceptance/invitation letter is posted to SAIA, n.o., Sasinkova 10, 812 20 Bratislava 1, Slovakia
The travel grant is requested within the scholarship application itself
official.application_route: Apply online at www.scholarships.sk (international track) or www.stipendia.sk (Slovak outgoing track) and post the original acceptance/invitation letter to SAIA in Bratislava
official.citizenship_residency: Incoming track: citizens of any country in the world except citizens of Slovakia. Outgoing track: students, doctoral candidates and postdoctoral staff of Slovak higher education institutions and research organisations with permanent residence in Slovakia (citizens of the Slovak Republic regardless of residence, EU/EEA/Swiss citizens with a right of residence, and third-country nationals with permanent or long-term residence)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the incoming track is open to applicants of any nationality except Slovak citizens, including students, PhD students, university teachers, researchers and artists hosted by a Slovak institution
official.research_requirement: PhD students, university teachers, researchers and artists must submit a detailed study/research/artistic (teaching) programme naming the host institution, start date, duration and an appropriately detailed time plan; PhD students and teachers also submit the publication/artistic activity list
official.duration: Incoming students: 1-2 full semesters (4-5 or 9-10 months) or 1-3 full trimesters; incoming PhD students, teachers, researchers and artists: 1-10 months. Outgoing track: study stay minimum 1 semester up to 1 academic year, doctoral stay 1-10 months, postdoctoral stay 2-6 months
official.description: The National Scholarship Programme of the Slovak Republic supports the mobility of students, PhD students, university teachers, researchers and artists; it is financed by the Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic from the state budget and administered by SAIA, n.o.
official.region: Slovakia (incoming stays); outgoing stays at foreign institutions worldwide
official.english_requirement: No IELTS/TOEFL score is published; applications and required attachments must be submitted in Slovak or English, and documents issued in Czech are accepted without translation

not_confirmed: Any host-institution-specific application deadline that differs from the programme deadline
Any English-language proficiency test requirement (no IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent score is published)
Accommodation provision, which depends on the individual Slovak host institution and is not guaranteed by SAIA
Exact calendar of the next round (30 April 2027) beyond the standing annual rule
verification.notes: Monthly amounts, coverage, eligibility rules, document lists and payment conditions were read directly from SAIA's programme terms pages for international and Slovak applicants; the outgoing country rate table was read in full; the current open call and its 31 October 2026 deadline were confirmed on the programme's news page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a living-cost stipend, not a full ride: the programme pays a fixed monthly rate (620 EUR for master's students, 1025.50 EUR for PhD students, up to 1470 EUR for senior researchers) plus a distance-based travel lump sum, while tuition stays on you. International applicants apply in Slovak or English through scholarships.sk, and the classic failure point is paper logistics - the original invitation letter must physically reach SAIA in Bratislava within three working days after the deadline. With only one application allowed per round and a two-year cooling-off period between awards, your host choice and stay dates need to be settled before you log in.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's and PhD students who already have a Slovak host willing to invite them for a 1-10 month mobility stay, and researchers/teachers invited by a Slovak research institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Obtain an acceptance/invitation letter from your Slovak host that covers exactly the stay dates you will request and is dated within 3 months of the deadline
Request an enrolment confirmation from your home university that is less than 3 months old on the deadline day
Collect two signed recommendation letters (students) or your supervisor's signed letter (PhD) showing the issuer's position and contact details
Arrange courier delivery of the original invitation letter to SAIA in Bratislava so it arrives by the 3rd working day after the deadline, before noon
Prepare a notarised copy of your highest diploma and a study confirmation valid for the academic year of the stay, since these gate the first monthly payment
common_rejection_risks: Formal rejection with no right to fix: SAIA does not give applicants a chance to amend, so a missing attachment or an out-of-date document sinks the file as submitted
Acceptance/invitation letter older than 3 months at the deadline, or not matching the stay period requested in the form
Applying for full-degree study in Slovakia, or having spent 15+ months in Slovakia in the 36 months before the deadline - both are automatic exclusions
Holding another publicly funded scholarship for the same stay (Erasmus+, Visegrad Fund, CEEPUS, bilateral agreements)
Contradictions between the application form and its attachments, which the administrator checks for and treats as formal defects
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees at the Slovak host, flights beyond the distance-based travel lump sum, visa and residence-permit fees, health insurance, and any living costs above the fixed monthly rate - the programme does not provide housing and only advises asking the host for help with accommodation
document_audit: Recommendation letters need a handwritten or verifiably electronic signature, the issuer's position and contact details, and institutional identification; unsigned letters are only tolerated in documented force-majeure cases and must be replaced before the award decree

Documents in languages other than Slovak or English (Czech exempted) need an official or institution-certified translation; applicant-made translations are accepted only in force-majeure situations and must be swapped for official ones before the Letter of Award

The invitation letter must name the host, the exact stay dates and, for study stays, ideally the subject list with ECTS credits - a generic one-liner weakens the application and risks a mismatch rejection
PhD, teacher and researcher applicants need the publication/artistic activity list in the prescribed structure, even if it is only a nil declaration
alerts: One application per deadline per applicant - a corrected or improved file cannot be resubmitted, so freeze the host and dates first
Re-applying is blocked until at least 2 years have passed since your last NSP award and completed stay, so a weak first attempt costs you a full cycle
No extensions and no change of host institution or country once awarded; shortening or date changes need SAIA's prior approval
The 31 October deadline feeds a stay starting from 1 February 2027, so visa and residence-permit lead times must be built into your arrival date
Up to one monthly stipend can be withheld until the final stay report and confirmation are submitted
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fill the online form at scholarships.sk, upload all attachments, press SEND before 31 October 2026 16:00 CET, then post the original invitation letter to SAIA in Bratislava for arrival within 3 working days; decisions are communicated roughly 8 weeks after the deadline
